title: Shopify vs BigCommerce for Ecommerce + POS: Plain-English Guide (2026)
summary: Compare Shopify vs BigCommerce for e-commerce and POS. Learn key differences in omnichannel retail, inventory sync, and zero-downtime migration.
body_markdown:
When comparing


**Shopify vs BigCommerce** for both online e-commerce and physical retail,


the decision boils down to one structural difference:


**Shopify provides a native, first-party Point of Sale (POS) out of the box** ,


whereas


**BigCommerce relies on third-party POS apps and connectors** (like Clover,


Square,


or Lightspeed) to sell in person.


If you want a


**unified commerce system** where online inventory,


physical store checkout,


pickup orders,


customer profiles,


and staff permissions run from a single admin dashboard,


**Shopify is the stronger, safer choice** .


**BigCommerce** remains a viable option for online-first merchants with complex,


B2B-heavy e-commerce catalogs who prefer assembling a separate retail tech stack using external middleware.

## **At-a-Glance Comparison: Shopify vs BigCommerce**


**Feature** **Shopify** **BigCommerce**


**Primary Focus**


Unified E-Commerce + Physical Retail (Omnichannel)


Online E-Commerce & Complex B2B Catalogs


**Native POS Solution?**


**Yes** (Shopify POS included; POS Pro add-on available)


**No** (Requires third-party apps or connectors)


**Inventory Management**


Built-in multi-location inventory across online + stores


Online inventory standard; retail sync depends on external POS


**Omnichannel Workflows**


Native Buy Online, Pick Up In-Store (BOPIS) & Ship-from-Store


Requires custom app integration or middleware


**App Ecosystem**


6,000+ apps (including 3,000+ free tools)


~1,200+ curated partner apps


**Payment Options**


Native Shopify Payments + Tap to Pay on iPhone/Android


Integrates with 55+ third-party payment gateways


**Best For**


Multi-location retailers, pop-ups, and scaling omnichannel brands


Online-only merchants or legacy brands needing decoupled POS systems


## **1. POS Model & Brick-and-Mortar Retail**


The fundamental operational difference lies in how each platform handles in-person selling.


- **Shopify’s POS Architecture:** Shopify treats retail as a core component of its platform.


Online sales and physical registers share the same product catalog,


order history,


customer profiles,


and real-time inventory counts.


Selling an item in-store instantly decrements online stock,


preventing accidental overselling.


- **BigCommerce’s POS Architecture:** BigCommerce relies on external POS software connected via APIs or sync bridges.


While this offers flexibility in choosing hardware vendors,


**connectors represent a potential point of failure** .


If an API sync lags or disconnects,


online and physical inventory drift out of alignment.


## **2. Omnichannel Workflows & Fulfillment**


Post-transaction workflows—such as local fulfillment,


returns,


and inventory routing—are where operational headaches typically emerge.


### **Native Shopify Workflows**


- **Buy Online, Pick Up In-Store (BOPIS):** Real-time stock display on product pages with automated fulfillment notifications for store staff.


- **Ship to Customer from POS:** Retail staff can process an out-of-stock item at the register and ship it directly from a central warehouse or another store.


- **Tap to Pay Integration:** Native support for


**Tap to Pay on iPhone and Android** in supported countries (including Canada and the US),


enabling instant line-busting without extra card terminals.


- **Unified Gift Cards & Customer Profiles:** Customers can buy a gift card online and redeem it at your physical cash register (or vice versa) without custom development.


### **BigCommerce Workflows**


While BigCommerce covers core storefront needs (hosting,


24/7 support,


multi-currency,


and checkout),


omnichannel features like store pickup,


local delivery,


and cross-channel gift cards require third-party apps or custom API extensions.


## **3. Shopify POS Depth: Included vs POS Pro**


Shopify offers two distinct retail feature levels depending on your store complexity:


```text
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    SHOPIFY RETAIL LAYERS                        │
├────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────┤
│    INCLUDED POS (All Plans)    │       POS PRO ADD-ON           │
│  • Hardware Support            │  • Unlimited POS Staff Logins  │
│  • Barcode Camera Scanning     │  • Exchanges & Cancellations   │
│  • Email / SMS Receipts        │  • Save & Email Carts          │
│  • Multi-Location Inventory    │  • Native BOPIS & Store Ship   │
│  • Staff PINs & Refunds        │  • Daily Register & Analytics  │
└────────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────┘


```


- **Included POS (All Paid Plans):** Perfect for pop-ups,


markets,


or simple single-counter retail.


Includes camera barcode scanning,


manual discounts,


custom digital receipts,


staff PINs,


and basic multi-location tracking.


- **Shopify POS Pro ($89/mo per location; ~ $67–$79 on annual terms):** Essential for busy brick-and-mortar storefronts.


Adds retail staff permissions,


unlimited POS-only staff logins,


order exchanges,


save/retrieve cart,


store pickup fulfillment,


receiving stock transfers,


and daily register closing reports.

## **4. App Ecosystem & Technical Extensibility**


With


**over 6,000 apps** (and more than 3,


000 free options),


Shopify’s ecosystem allows merchants to scale operations without custom coding:


- **Channel Expansion:** One-click syncing to marketplaces like Amazon,


eBay,


and Whatnot.


- **Marketing & ERP Sync:** Direct integrations for Klaviyo,


ERPs (Netsuite,


SAP),


and accounting tools (QuickBooks,


Xero).


- **Migration Tooling:** Automated data migration utilities to cleanly import product tags,


customer records,


and blog content from legacy systems like BigCommerce.


## **5. How to Migrate from BigCommerce to Shopify**


When transitioning from BigCommerce to Shopify,


maintaining data integrity requires a strict execution order:


### **Recommended Migration Sequence**


1. **Import Product & Catalog Data First:** Establish SKUs,


variants,


product descriptions,


and multi-location inventory stock levels.


2. **Import Customer Profiles Second:** Link existing records to preserve purchase history and email preferences.


3. **Import Historical Orders Third:** Map historical order data so returning customers and support staff retain complete order context.


4. **Configure 301 Redirects:** Map every legacy BigCommerce URL path to its new Shopify equivalent to protect your search engine rankings.


5. **Hardware & Staff Provisioning:** Configure POS card readers,


barcode scanners,


staff PINs,


and inventory permissions before opening day.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **Can BigCommerce connect to a retail POS system?**


Yes.


BigCommerce can connect to third-party POS systems (such as Clover,


Square,


or Lightspeed) via third-party integration apps.


However,


it does not offer a native,


first-party POS built into its core admin.


### **Will migrating from BigCommerce to Shopify affect my search engine rankings?**


Not if executed properly.


By mapping 100% of your old BigCommerce URLs to your new Shopify URLs using proper 301 redirects,


preserving page metadata,


and maintaining clean schema data,


your SEO rankings will remain protected.


### **Do I need a separate card processing terminal for Shopify POS?**


No.


You can use Shopify’s dedicated hardware (like the Shopify POS Terminal or POS Go) or use


**Tap to Pay on iPhone/Android** directly through the Shopify POS app without additional card terminals.


## **Final Verdict: Which Platform Should You Choose?**


- **Choose Shopify if:** You operate physical stores,


pop-ups,


or showrooms and want a unified operating model.


Shopify gives you a native POS,


shared inventory,


store pickup,


and predictable retail management out of the box.


- **Choose BigCommerce if:** You operate an online-only e-commerce business with complex wholesale/B2B quoting rules,


and in-person retail is either non-existent or completely secondary to your business model.
